factors.name: Connector branching / connectivity
factors.summary: Very high loadings of average and maximum connector degree, token split, arcs per node and control flow complexity show that this factor captures how many arcs meet at connectors, i.e. branching density of the control flow. Number of empty sequence flows (0.75, also 0.43 on Factor 3) and Connector Mismatch (0.56, also 0.38 on Factor 4) load more moderately. With 50% of the variance it is the dominant factor.

factors.name: Size and separability
factors.summary: Size (0.85) and Separability (0.82) load highly, so larger nets in this dataset also tend to have a larger share of non-articulation nodes. Size also loads 0.45 on Factor 1, and Sequentiality loads 0.50 here, but below its main loading. The factor rests on only two clear measures, and Separability has a low MSA (0.61).

factors.name: Sequentiality / connector mix
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.79) and Connector Heterogeneity (0.66) load on this factor, with Number of empty sequence flows at 0.43. The factor may reflect how the arcs split between sequential and connector parts and how parallel and choice connectors are mixed. However, the shared meaning of these measures is not obvious, and Connector Heterogeneity has a low communality (0.46).

factors.name: Weak residual factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor. It explains only 2.6% of the variance, and its largest loading is Connector Mismatch at 0.38, which is secondary to that measure's Factor 1 loading. It should not be interpreted substantively.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett significant, KMO 0.81), and the four factors explain 86% of the variance. The structure is dominated by a connector branching and connectivity factor (50%). Smaller factors capture net size with separability (19%) and sequentiality with connector heterogeneity (14%). Only two eigenvalues exceed 1 and two factors were suggested, so the extraction of four factors leaves Factor 4 empty and Factor 3 only partly supported. Density was removed by the MSA filter and Number of duplicate tasks was removed as a constant.
caveats: Four factors were extracted although two were suggested, so Factor 4 is an empty overextraction and Factor 3 has an eigenvalue below 1.
Coefficient of network connectivity shows a possible Heywood case (uniqueness ≤ 0.005), which may distort the solution.
Factors 2 and 3 each rest on only two measures, which limits how firmly they can be named.
Density and Number of duplicate tasks were excluded, so they are not represented in any factor.
The results reflect shared variance among these 288 discovered nets under varimax rotation, not causal dimensions.
